item.title: Extragalactic Archaeology: A New Method To Understand Galaxy Growth and Evolution
item.description: Galactic archaeology uses chemical fingerprints in the Milky Way to trace its formation and evolution. Now a team of researchers led by the Center for Astrophysics | Harvard and Smithsonian have employed it for the first time in a distant galaxy. This is the first example of extragalactic archaeology, and it relies on help from the powerful Illustris TNG simulations.

item.title: NASA Lays Out Ambitious Plans for Moon Base and Nuclear Mars Mission
item.description: NASA has outlined an ambitious strategy to start working on a moon base and send a nuclear-powered spacecraft to Mars by the end of 2028 — leading some observers to wonder whether the timeline was realistic or wise.

item.title: Mars Plant Growth from Cyanobacteria-Based Fertilizer
item.description: You’re the Lead Botanist on the third human mission to Mars whose primary job involves growing food for the crew throughout the long mission. While you’re very familiar with the infamous “poop potatoes” from the 2025 film The Martian, the greatest minds in science had since devised a more efficient, and less messy, method for growing food on Mars: cyanobacteria.

item.description: The planet Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun, and also the most difficult for spacecraft to visit and explore. This is because as spacecraft get closer to Mercury, the Sunâs enormous gravity pulls in the spacecraft, greatly increasing its speed and making it hard to slow down without large amounts of fuel.
